source_acquisition.search_note: The automated inventory was partial and the local LoongRL checkout contained only evaluation.yaml. I verified the author-linked LoongRL repository with gh, found no figure/table generators there, then verified the linked KeyChain repository and its two plotting notebooks. The author arXiv source package (ID 2510.19363) contains the exact TeX inclusions and embedded PDF assets for every Figure plus the table/caption source, so the final status is exact_visual_source; repository-without-visual-source and local-source limitations remain recorded in the evidence.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Three coordinated visual palettes: black/white booktabs tables with light teal Avg/Overall cells; blue–orange–green stage curves and boundaries; and diagram/heatmap accents using blue, orange, teal and pink→yellow→teal accuracy. Labels, panel position, rules and text provide partial redundancy, but heatmap magnitude depends primarily on color.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Single-column Letter PDF is vector-first: LaTeX text/tables/tcolorboxes and imported source PDFs remain vector, while heatmap/image XObjects and embedded Type3 plot assets make the final objects mixed. Font embedding is heterogeneous across author diagrams and Matplotlib assets.
paper_style.style_consistency: Float placement, caption syntax, booktabs rules and grouped headers are consistent. Typography is only subsystem-consistent (Nimbus/CM for paper, Arial/Aptos for diagrams, DejaVuSans for plots); color semantics are more stable than font identity. No object uses an uncertainty band/error bar.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Model trajectories on long-context multi-hop QA with and without KeyChain RL data. (a) With KeyChain data, model exhibits an emergent plan–retrieve–reason–recheck thinking pattern, improving reasoning reliability and can generalize to longer contexts. (b) Without KeyChain data, reasoning and retrieval are entangled, the model often lacks an explicit planning step and does not deeply reason over retrieved information, frequently leading to errors. Reasoning steps are marked in blue and retrieval steps in orange.

color.semantic_mapping: blue marks reasoning; orange marks retrieval; boxes/status colors distinguish planning, checking, success and error; panel position gives the matched trajectory comparison.

encodings.text: plan, retrieve, reason, recheck text and answer status

figures.data_and_statistics: Representative traces for one long-context multi-hop QA setting, not a population sample. The left trace contains explicit planning, retrieval, reasoning and rechecking; the right trace interleaves retrieval and reasoning and ends in an error. No frequency, denominator, run count or uncertainty is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: The introduction and Appendix A.4 mechanism claim → Figure 1 matched qualitative contrast → Table 5 equal-data no-KeyChain ablation → F4/F7/F8 training dynamics. The trace illustrates the proposed mediator but does not establish its prevalence.
design_strengths: Same-question left/right contrast makes the proposed reasoning pattern immediately inspectable.
Arrow order, colored step text, panel titles and answer status provide redundant structure cues.
The caption names both the comparison and the blue/orange encoding.
design_weaknesses: Dense text and small embedded labels become hard to read at single-column width.
A few hand-selected traces cannot quantify behavior frequency or causal mediation.
Blue/orange categories are not fully robust in grayscale and no sampling rule is given.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a matched task and two horizontally aligned trajectories to expose a mechanism; pair it with a quantitative ablation and state the trace sampling denominator.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Overview of our KeyChain data construction.

color.semantic_mapping: orange/blue/teal stage cards encode filtering, context filling and UUID-chain insertion; arrows and document icons encode transformations and target/distractor roles.

encodings.text: step numbers, UUIDs, target and distractor question text

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual construction flow: 277K seed multi-hop QA are filtered using eight Qwen2.5-32B responses to about 72K moderate examples, filled with distractor documents to below 16,384 tokens, and augmented with random-position 32-character UUID chains. The diagram gives no per-stage retention rate, failure count or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Method §3.1 and Table 1 recipe → Figure 2 three-stage interface → Figure 6 concrete skeleton → T5/T9 component and UUID ablations. It explains how the data component is supposed to induce the trace in Figure 1.
design_strengths: Three isomorphic step cards give a clear left-to-right reading order.
Input, operation and output roles are visible without requiring a numerical axis.
Document icons, arrows and labels redundantly encode the transformation.
design_weaknesses: Many labels and icons are small and the caption gives no filtering counts.
Pastel/blue/orange category colors carry substantial hierarchy and weaken in grayscale.
The figure does not show discarded examples or quality gates, so the data-flow loss is invisible.
figures.reusable_pattern: Represent a data transformation as filtering → length expansion → structural insertion, with a count and an explicit rejection branch at each stage.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Needle in a Haystack retrieval across document depths. The base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct does not fully pass the benchmark, whereas LoongRL-7B achieves perfect 100% retrieval accuracy.

color.semantic_mapping: pink→yellow→teal maps NIAH accuracy from 0 to 1; white cell boundaries and panel titles delimit bins.

encodings.text: model names, rotated bin labels and 0–1 colorbars

figures.data_and_statistics: Each cell is retrieval accuracy for a context-length × document-depth bin in the NIAH stress test. LoongRL-7B is visually all 1.0; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B becomes mostly zero after roughly 20K; Qwen2.5-7B and QwenLong-L1-32B retain mostly high values. Cell sample sizes, seeds, repeated-run dispersion and failure counts are absent.
figures.evidence_relation: The abstract/main-results 16K→128K and retrieval claims → Table 4 length results → Figure 3 7B depth/length stress test → Appendix Figure 9 14B extension and Table 8 RULER sweep. The heatmap supports a bounded benchmark claim, not a universal retrieval guarantee.
design_strengths: Two-dimensional bins reveal both length and depth failure boundaries rather than hiding them in one average.
Common panel geometry makes model differences easy to scan.
The caption states the central 7B comparison and outcome.
design_weaknesses: Four independent colorbars and a continuous palette add visual load.
Color is the primary value channel and is not reliably grayscale safe.
No cell denominator or uncertainty prevents interpreting a uniform green field as a guarantee.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched length × depth heatmaps with one shared colorbar, explicit per-cell n, and a caption that states the tested protocol and boundary.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Long-context reasoning accuracy and training response lengths throughout RL training.

color.semantic_mapping: blue/orange/green identify Warmup, Stage 1 and Stage 2; gray dashed lines identify stage transitions; panel title and legend redundantly state stages.

encodings.shape: score markers versus no markers for response length
encodings.line: solid trajectories and dashed stage boundaries

figures.data_and_statistics: Four training trajectories: LB1 average score and average response length over steps for 7B and 14B. 7B uses Warmup/Stage 1/Stage 2 and 14B uses Stage 1/Stage 2. Curves are point trajectories; no run count, seed, confidence/dispersion band, or GPU-hour measure is shown, and response length is only a proxy for generation burden.
figures.evidence_relation: Ablation/curriculum prose and T1 recipe → Figure 4 training trajectory → Appendix F7/F8 per-metric diagnostics → T5 KeyChain ablation and T2/T4 outcomes. It diagnoses when learning changes, not why a component is causally sufficient.
design_strengths: Shared step axis places quality and response-length dynamics in one view.
Stage boundaries align curriculum changes with observable trajectories.
The color legend and panel titles permit model/metric comparison.
design_weaknesses: Single trajectories do not show run-to-run variation or reproducibility.
Different metric scales and separate legends make cross-panel magnitude comparison difficult.
Response length is not compute, memory or latency and is not a cost outcome.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair quality with a process proxy on a common training-step axis and mark curriculum boundaries; add run aggregation and measured compute in a production version.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: System prompt used during training

color.semantic_mapping: gray title bar and borders separate the system prompt, while monospace tags and indentation identify the parser-facing syntax.

figures.data_and_statistics: A reproduced training system prompt, including the reasoning-tag convention and final \boxed{} answer requirement. It is an interface artifact rather than a sample or aggregate statistic; the figure does not report prompt versioning, parser coverage or failure rates.
figures.evidence_relation: GRPO reward definition in §3.2.1 → Figure 5 exact prompt → Table 6 verifier alternatives. The prompt is needed to reproduce answer extraction but does not itself establish verifier quality.
design_strengths: Places the parser-critical prompt in a copyable, visually bounded artifact.
Monospace tags and box hierarchy make syntax distinct from prose.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not explain its dependency on the boxed-answer verifier.
Small code text after scaling can be difficult to transcribe; no parser/version metadata is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show the exact prompt next to its parser contract and version, rather than treating a prompt screenshot as a performance result.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: A skeleton of KeyChain-augmented training data used in LoongRL.

color.semantic_mapping: teal header and dark containers define the skeleton; orange UUID/question tokens and green/white status fields distinguish chain content and answer roles.

encodings.text: field labels, UUIDs and question text

figures.data_and_statistics: A schema skeleton for one KeyChain-augmented record: distractor documents, UUID key/value links, a hidden target question and final answer fields. It demonstrates field relationships but is not a random sample, complete dataset, length distribution or count of generated records.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2 construction pipeline → Figure 6 concrete record interface → Table 1 corpus recipe and Table 9 UUID-format ablation. It provides reproduction context for the data component tested in T5.
design_strengths: Shows schema, chain traversal and target/distractor roles in one artifact.
Borders and field labels provide structure independent of the accent colors.
design_weaknesses: A skeleton may hide variation and does not state which fields are optional or repeated.
No example-level token count, generation rule or corpus coverage is given.
figures.reusable_pattern: Combine a schema skeleton with one fully instantiated chain and explicit target/distractor labels; include schema version and length statistics.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Training metrics for the three-stage schedule. Vertical dashed lines mark the transitions Warmup → Stage II (distractor-augmented) and Stage II → Stage III (hard-mined); stage lengths correspond to our setup (about 42, 168, and 117 steps).

color.semantic_mapping: blue/orange/green identify the three stages; gray dashed vertical lines mark stage transitions; panel titles and direct labels repeat the metric meaning.

encodings.y: consistent predictions, reward or response length

figures.data_and_statistics: Per-step 7B diagnostics for consistent predictions per batch, average reward and average response length across the three-stage schedule. Values are process trajectories; the source does not give seed aggregation, number of batches per point, uncertainty or a direct cost measure.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 4 summarizes the same 7B schedule → Figure 7 expands its three diagnostics → T1 gives data mix and T5 measures the KeyChain component. The curves are compatible with a curriculum-change interpretation but do not identify a causal mediator.
design_strengths: Three metrics share a step axis and make curriculum transitions explicit.
A shared legend and direct stage labels reduce repeated decoding.
design_weaknesses: The caption’s Stage II/III naming requires mapping to the main-text stage names.
No run-level variation or batch denominator is shown; response length remains a proxy.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a three-panel process diagnostic with shared x-axis and vertical stage markers, but report batch/run aggregation and measured compute beside the length proxy.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Training metrics for the LoongRL-14B’s two-stage schedule. Vertical dashed lines mark the transitions Stage I (distractor-augmented) and → Stage III (hard-mined); stage lengths correspond to our setup (about 168, and 150 steps).

color.semantic_mapping: orange/green identify the two stages and gray marks the transition; panel titles and stage labels provide textual redundancy.

encodings.y: consistent predictions, reward or response length

figures.data_and_statistics: Per-step 14B diagnostics for the same three metrics as Figure 7, with a two-stage schedule and one transition near step 168. The plotted values are point trajectories without seeds, run aggregation, sample counts, uncertainty or direct hardware-cost measurement.
figures.evidence_relation: The 14B panel in Figure 4 → Figure 8 schedule expansion → T2/T4 14B results and T1 recipe. It supports the descriptive claim that 14B omits warmup, but the figure alone cannot attribute final quality to the stage boundary.
design_strengths: Shares metric order and plot grammar with Figure 7, enabling scale comparison.
One common transition and shared legend keep the two-stage schedule legible.
design_weaknesses: Caption has the source typo `and → Stage III` and does not clearly name the second transition.
Two stage nomenclatures across main text/caption add mapping cost; no uncertainty or compute.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a fixed metric order across model-size schedules and normalize stage naming; add explicit transition labels and replicate/run bands.

figures.label: Figure 9

color.semantic_mapping: the shared pink→yellow→teal scale maps 14B NIAH accuracy across context length and document depth; white cells delimit bins.

figures.data_and_statistics: A single LoongRL-14B NIAH accuracy heatmap over 15 context-length and 10 depth bins. Cells are near 1 with one slight variation; cell n, run variation, seed and uncertainty are not shown, so this is a bounded stress-test result rather than a universal guarantee.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix extension of Figure 3’s 7B heatmaps → Table 4/T8 length sweeps → the 16K training to 128K inference claim. It closes the missing 14B visual slice while retaining the same protocol limitations.
design_strengths: Reuses Figure 3 axes and color semantics for direct 7B/14B comparison.
Inset avoids consuming a full page while preserving the 2-D stress-test structure.
design_weaknesses: Inset scale makes labels and colorbar small.
A nearly uniform field offers little quantitative resolution and lacks per-cell denominators.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use the same heatmap geometry and scale for an appendix model extension, with a shared legend and explicit cell counts to make uniform success interpretable.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Data recipe for long-context RL training.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty column; sizes and length ranges are recipe counts, not repeated-run estimates.
tables.data_and_statistics: Ten body rows list each training subset’s dataset/description, size, token-length range and Hard/Medium/Easy difficulty. Values such as 2,500, 512 and 40–20,670 are exact point counts/ranges; there are no retention rates, rejected-example counts, seeds or dispersion statistics.
tables.evidence_relation: Method §3.2.2 defines the 16K mixed-data recipe → Table 1 fixes the dataset boundary → F4/F7/F8 show training schedule and T2–T4 report outcomes. The table is the denominator/context needed to interpret the curriculum and ablations.
design_strengths: Combines subset identity, size, length and difficulty in a compact scan.
Booktabs grouping keeps the recipe readable without a full grid.
design_weaknesses: Long descriptions and no filter-loss columns conceal how the final mix was obtained.
Row-group semantics depend on horizontal rules rather than explicit group headers.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a minimal recipe table with dataset, count, length and difficulty, adding retained/rejected counts and total tokens for auditability.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Results of LoongRL and frontier LLMs on long-context reasoning and general short tasks. LoongRL delivers frontier-level long-context reasoning at much smaller scales (7B/14B), rivaling o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1, while preserving general short-context abilities across all scales.

tables.uncertainty: All entries are point average pass@1/percentage values; no run-level uncertainty, seed, task sample count or cost column is provided.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen model rows span frontier, distilled and LoongRL models. Eleven logical columns group long-context reasoning and General & Short Reasoning; LoongRL-7B and LoongRL-14B average 72.4 and 74.2, while o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1 are 74.5 and 74.9. Each score is one decimal and the Avg column is light teal; best/second-best cells use bold/underline.
tables.evidence_relation: Abstract gains and 74.2 headline → Table 2 main comparison → T3 HELMET, T4 length generalization, F3/F9 retrieval and T5 KeyChain ablation. The grouped header prevents short-task columns from being conflated with long-context scores, but the “all scales” caption wording is broader than the two trained LoongRL rows.
design_strengths: Grouped headers separate long-context and short-task decisions.
Teal Avg plus bold/underline makes the headline ranking fast to locate.
Per-task columns retain some heterogeneity instead of only reporting one average.
design_weaknesses: Eleven columns force small type and dense header wrapping.
Average values hide task weighting and no uncertainty or compute-normalized comparator is present.
Caption states a broad preservation claim without listing protocol or sample denominators.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped benchmark families with an emphasized Avg, but include task n, evaluation protocol and matched compute/uncertainty alongside the point estimates.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Results of LoongRL and frontier LLMs on the HELMET long-context generation benchmark. LoongRL-7B and LoongRL-14B substantially outperform baseline models.

tables.uncertainty: Point scores only; no uncertainty, per-subtask n, generation-length/cost measure or failure breakdown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seven body rows and nine logical columns group RAG, Generation with Citations and Summarization. The average scores for LoongRL-7B and LoongRL-14B are 44.8 and 49.0; subtask values are one decimal, with light-teal Avg and bold LoongRL emphasis.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends T2’s QA comparison to HELMET generation → Table 3 tests RAG/citation/summarization → T4/F3/F9 cover retrieval and length stress. It broadens the utility claim but does not supply a matched compute or uncertainty comparison.
design_strengths: Grouped task families preserve the semantics of different generation tests.
Average column and bold rows make the claimed LoongRL improvement visible.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not define score direction, task count or evaluation protocol.
No uncertainty, failure category or cost prevents decision-level comparison.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use benchmark-family group headers and an Avg column, while placing task definitions, sample counts and protocol asymmetries in a compact caption or note.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: While being trained only on 16K, LoongRL generalizes impressively to context up to 128K.

tables.uncertainty: Point accuracies/percentages only; no sample count, seed or run dispersion, hardware cost or protocol-asymmetry column.
tables.data_and_statistics: Eight body rows compare models on three NarrativeQA length buckets and four RULER length buckets under two grouped headers. LoongRL-7B has NarrativeQA 69.8/47.4/57.2 and RULER 93.4/91.4/86.2/76.8; LoongRL-14B has 69.5/55.2/64.3 and 95.4/95.1/87.1/79.9. All displayed values use one decimal; a source spacer column carries no visible data.
tables.evidence_relation: Direct evidence for the 16K-training → 128K-evaluation claim → F3/F9 NIAH heatmaps provide depth slices → Appendix T8 expands RULER lengths and protocol. It does not measure the counterfactual full-length RL cost.
design_strengths: Length buckets are columns, so degradation/generalization is visible without an opaque single average.
NarrativeQA and RULER are explicitly separated by two-level headers.
design_weaknesses: Different benchmarks and prompt protocols complicate direct cross-group reading.
No uncertainty, denominator or cost column and the blank source spacer can confuse reconstruction.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate training-window and evaluation-length groups in one table, explicitly marking protocol changes, cell n and the counterfactual cost baseline.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Ablation study on the effectiveness of KeyChain data.

tables.uncertainty: Point average pass@1 values only; no seed, uncertainty, task n or failed-verifier breakdown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three rows compare Qwen base, LoongRL-7B without KeyChain and full LoongRL on five long-context QA datasets plus Avg. Avg increases from 48.9 to 66.2 to 72.4; all values use one decimal, the Avg column is teal and the full row is bold.
tables.evidence_relation: KeyChain component hypothesis → T5 matched three-row replacement → Figure 1 qualitative mechanism and T2 headline. It is the clearest numerical link from data construction to improvement, subject to the stated equal-setting control.
design_strengths: Base→removed component→full structure isolates a central design choice.
Five task columns and Avg show whether the gain is broad rather than only one benchmark.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not specify equal data size or which training variables are held fixed.
Only point estimates are shown, so small task-specific differences lack reproducibility context.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact base/removed/full ablation with identical task columns and state the controlled replacement directly in the caption.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Ablation study on the different answer verifiers on the 7B.

tables.uncertainty: Downstream point scores only; no verifier precision/recall, parse coverage, failure type, latency, seed or uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four Reward Verifier rows (F1, LLM-as-a-judge, Exact match, Two-way Substring Exact Match) span five tasks plus Avg. Average values are 65.1, 65.2, 69.2 and 72.4 respectively; one decimal, teal Avg and bold best/ours cells. This evaluates the verifier through downstream RL, not an independent verifier accuracy test.
tables.evidence_relation: §3.2.1 boxed-answer and two-way substring reward → T6 verifier replacement ablation → Figure 5 prompt reproduction and T2/T5 downstream scores. It supports the practical choice but not verifier correctness as a standalone measurement.
design_strengths: Keeps task set and model fixed while exposing the reward-parser choice.
Rows and Avg make the selected substring verifier easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: Judge cost and failure semantics are absent, and “on the 7B” is imprecise.
No uncertainty or parser coverage means downstream differences may be hard to reproduce.
tables.reusable_pattern: Compare reward/verifier implementations under one fixed recipe and report both downstream outcome and independent parsing coverage/cost.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7: Comparison of LoongRL models with other baselines on the LongBench-v2 benchmark, grouped by Difficulty, Length, and Task Type.

tables.uncertainty: Avg@5 point averages; no per-task n, run/seed dispersion, uncertainty, cost or failure category.
tables.data_and_statistics: Twelve body rows and thirteen columns report Overall plus two Difficulty, three Length and six Task Type slices. Frontier, 7B and 14B row blocks are separated by rules; Overall is teal and best cells are bold/underlined. The table is an aggregate LongBench-v2 view, not raw task-level counts.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix extension of T2 LongBench-v1 → T7 slices performance by difficulty, length and task type → main headline and T4 length generalization. The additional axes expose heterogeneity but retain the aggregation limits of T2.
design_strengths: Orthogonal slices expose where a model’s overall score comes from.
Two-level grouped headers preserve the meaning of 13 dense columns.
design_weaknesses: Thirteen columns are compressed and Avg@5 is not explained in the caption.
No task denominators or uncertainty makes slice differences difficult to assess.
tables.reusable_pattern: Present Overall beside orthogonal difficulty/length/task slices and define the aggregation (including k/pass protocol) plus n for every slice.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8: RULER benchmark results across different context lengths. For QwQ, QwenLong, Qwen2.5 model series, we report their YaRN variants for 64k and 128k.

tables.uncertainty: RULER point scores by length; no per-length sample n, seeds, dispersion, cost or failure count. YaRN variants and suffix/think extraction create protocol boundaries that are not columns.
tables.data_and_statistics: Sixteen model rows span 4K, 8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 128K and Avg. values; model series are separated by horizontal rules, Avg is teal and best cells bold, with two decimal places. Caption marks YaRN for specified baselines at 64K/128K; Appendix A.8 also changes suffix/think extraction by model family.
tables.evidence_relation: T4’s compact length comparison → T8 full RULER length sweep and protocol details → F3/F9 retrieval heatmaps. It supplies more length points but direct cross-model comparisons remain bounded by YaRN and output-extraction differences.
design_strengths: A wide-length header makes degradation visible across six context sizes.
Model-family rules, precision and Avg emphasis support quick scanning.
design_weaknesses: Sixteen rows by eight columns make labels small.
Protocol asymmetry is in prose rather than the table, and no sample/cost/uncertainty fields are provided.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a context-length sweep table with explicit model/checkpoint and protocol columns, marking YaRN and extraction rules inline rather than in a distant appendix paragraph.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9: Analysis of the design choice of KeyChain data. The RL experiments are conducted on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

tables.uncertainty: Point average pass@1 values only; no randomization replicates, seed, uncertainty or chain-length distribution.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two rows compare UUID Reported and Random String on five tasks plus Avg in the same Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct RL setting. Avg values are 72.4 and 72.2; all scores have one decimal, Avg is teal and the UUID row is bold.
tables.evidence_relation: F2’s high-entropy/non-semantic chain rationale → T9 same-length random-string substitution → T5 KeyChain efficacy and F1 mechanism. The near-equal averages bound the claim to this one format substitution rather than all identifiers.
design_strengths: Minimal two-row format ablation keeps task coverage fixed.
The small difference is visible without a distracting chart.
design_weaknesses: One random-string condition and point estimates cannot establish equivalence over formats or seeds.
Caption does not state the same-length/control details needed to interpret the substitution.
tables.reusable_pattern: For representation-format claims, use same-task substitution rows and report multiple random draws, structural equivalence and uncertainty.

tables.label: Table 10

caption.text: Table 10: Example responses of LoongRL-14B at different RL training steps, showing how retrieval, reasoning, rechecking, and planning behaviors evolve over training.

tables.uncertainty: Examples use integer response lengths and binary ✓/× accuracy, but no sampling frame, annotator agreement, skill prevalence, seed or uncertainty is reported.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seven checkpoint rows have Stage, checkpoint/training step, Response Length, Skills and Accuracy. Stage 1 steps 10/20/70/118 have lengths 2,228/2,963/5,685/6,101 and move from Retrieve+Reason × to Retrieve+Reason+Recheck ✓; Stage 2 steps 199/229/319 have lengths 1,480/2,596/4,143 and show Plan+Retrieve+Reason(+Recheck) ✓. Skills are hand-coded examples, not a population statistic.
tables.evidence_relation: F4/F7/F8 training dynamics → T10 checkpoint examples → F1/A.4/A.5 plan–retrieve–reason–recheck narrative. It gives concrete qualitative support for an evolving skill story but cannot establish frequency or causal mediation.
design_strengths: Checkpoint ordering turns a qualitative skill claim into a compact temporal narrative.
The Accuracy and Skills columns link visible behavior to task outcome.
design_weaknesses: Manual example selection and skill labels are not operationalized.
A single example per checkpoint cannot support population frequency or intervention claims.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use checkpoint × observable skill × outcome rows, but disclose the sampling/annotation protocol and add cohort-level prevalence beside examples.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: KeyChain construction (Figure 2) → data recipe (Table 1) → headline comparisons (Tables 2–3) → 16K-to-128K length/retrieval evidence (Table 4, Figures 3 and 9) → training dynamics (Figure 4, Figures 7–8) → component/verifier/format ablations (Tables 5–6 and 9), with prompt/schema and checkpoint examples (Figures 5–6 and Table 10) supplying reproducibility and mechanism context.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every caption starts with Figure/Table n and sits below its object. Figure 1, Figure 3, Tables 2–4 state comparisons or findings; Figures 7–8 state setup and stage encoding; most other captions are title-only. Captions rarely define cell n, uncertainty, cost, protocol asymmetry or control variables, so many objects are not self-contained.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Booktabs top/mid/bottom rules and no vertical rules form the shared table grammar. Multi-level headers group benchmark family, difficulty, length and task type; light teal Avg/Overall columns and bold/underline best cells create a stable scan path. None of the tables has a dedicated uncertainty, cost or failure column.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 and Table 1 make the data interface and training mix explicit; Tables 5, 6 and 9 then replace KeyChain data, answer verifier and UUID format under the same task framing. Figure 1 and Figures 5–6 explain the qualitative/parser mechanism, while Tables 2–4 quantify downstream performance and generalization.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Appendix Figure 9 extends main Figure 3 from 7B to 14B; Table 8 expands main Table 4’s length sweep and adds protocol notes; Figures 7–8 expand Figure 4; Figure 5/Figure 6 and Table 10 supply prompt, schema and checkpoint examples behind the main mechanism. A.8 protocol details are necessary for interpreting RULER comparisons.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Paper text and captions use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern, imported diagrams use Arial/Aptos/CambriaMath, and Matplotlib assets use DejaVuSans Type3. Within each asset family the hierarchy is stable, but the mixed families and scaling produce small labels in single-column placement.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Light teal #D3E9E8 consistently marks Avg/Overall table columns; #1F77B4/#FF7F0E/#2CA02C consistently mark training stages; diagrams reuse blue/orange/teal accents; Figures 3/9 share the #F0496E→#EBB839→#0CD79F heatmap. The table and curve systems are partly grayscale-safe; heatmap values are not.

most_reusable_patterns: Matched same-task trajectory contrast to make a claimed reasoning mediator visible (Figure 1).
Three-stage data transformation pipeline with explicit input/output roles (Figure 2).
Grouped benchmark columns with teal Avg/Overall and bold/underline best values (Tables 2, 3 and 7).
Length-sweep tables paired with depth×length heatmaps for bounded long-context generalization (Table 4, Figure 3, Figure 9).
Matched component substitutions for data, verifier and identifier format (Tables 5, 6 and 9).
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 is the shortest mechanism evidence for plan–retrieve–reason–recheck versus entangled traces.
Figure 2 is the clearest method interface for KeyChain construction.
Table 2 is the headline multi-task comparison; Table 4 and Figures 3/9 establish the tested length/retrieval boundary.
Tables 5 and 6 are the most decision-relevant component ablations; Figure 4/7/8 are process diagnostics rather than final efficacy evidence.
failure_patterns: All numerical tables, heatmaps and training curves omit run-level uncertainty or cell denominators.
Average columns compress heterogeneous tasks and no object places performance beside compute, memory or failure cost.
Caption self-containment is weak for prompt, heatmap bins, verifier controls and RULER/YaRN extraction protocol.
Figure 1 and Table 10 use representative/manual traces without sampling or annotation rules, so they cannot support behavior prevalence.
The 16K training versus 128K inference cost claim lacks a full-length RL GPU-hour/memory quality control; Figure 8 caption retains the malformed `and → Stage III` phrase.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Make the KeyChain data transformation and matched trajectories explicit first, align grouped headline/length tables and depth×length heatmaps with controlled ablations, then use appendix prompt, dynamics and checkpoint artifacts to state reproducibility boundaries without treating illustrative examples as population statistics.
